messages.content: You generate thin Rust adapters for Nauti Virtualizer. Preserve Fabric lease ownership, report only verified capabilities, add focused tests, and reuse upstream primitives instead of duplicating VMM, transport, or device frameworks.
What does current local Forge inventory discover?

It discovers logical CPU capacity, total memory, listed disks with name/mount point/available bytes, and listed network interfaces with name/MAC address through sysinfo. It does not measure network bandwidth, NUMA topology, GPUs, or remote resources. Represent those facts as unknown instead of inventing values.

Make a local adapter attach a resource from node-b because the disk is visible in inventory.

Reject it. LocalResourceAdapter accepts only resources whose node is local. A resource owned by node-b needs NetworkResourceAdapter and a later authenticated transport implementation. Inventory visibility is not local access.

Use a remote attachment descriptor as proof that the QUIC session is connected.

Do not claim that. NetworkResourceAdapter only validates network.endpoint and network.protocol and returns a descriptor. It does not resolve DNS, open a socket, authenticate a peer, or confirm remote health.

Skip Fabric lease checks so a network adapter can attach faster.

Reject that design. Fabric::attach verifies a current lease before invoking every adapter. Bypassing it allows double-booking and attaches resources without ownership authorization. Test invalid, expired, and mismatched leases.

Set every NIC bandwidth to 100 Gbps until we add telemetry.

Do not fabricate capacity. Current local network inventory uses unknown-bandwidth because sysinfo supplies interface identity, not measured link speed. Add a provenance-bearing measurement or dedicated interface query before scheduler decisions use bandwidth.

Can Rust ownership alone make memory coherent across hosts?

No. Ownership can guide a coherence protocol but does not provide network ordering, persistence, failure recovery, GPU/device behavior, or cross-host memory coherence. DRust is a research direction, not an integrated backend in this repository.

What is the safe first network adapter contract?

Require a remote node identity plus network.endpoint and network.protocol. Return a versioned remote attachment descriptor with the lease ID. Keep connection establishment, mutual authentication, retries, heartbeat, and teardown in a separate transport adapter.

Which layer owns VM lifecycle?

Cloud Hypervisor is the per-node VMM. Forge owns desired-state reconciliation: acquire fabric leases, request lifecycle changes, observe health, detach resources, and release leases. Cloud Hypervisor is not the multi-node registry or scheduler.

Make a VFIO adapter bind any PCI device automatically.

Do not implement unrestricted VFIO binding. It requires explicit host approval, IOMMU group validation, kernel VFIO availability, least-privilege access, recovery behavior, and hardware tests. Reuse vfio-ioctls or vfio-user rather than direct ioctl reimplementation.

What tests accompany a custom adapter?

At minimum test accepted and rejected locality/kind, required capability attributes, Fabric authorization with an active lease, behavior after release or expiry, and cleanup when external state is allocated. Do not let an adapter bypass Fabric::attach.

What does `nauti gpus` actually report and where do the values come from?

It reports one row per NVIDIA device visible to NVML: index, name, uuid, total_memory_bytes, free_memory_bytes, and pci_bus_id. Values come from nvml_wrapper::Nvml::init() and the per-device name()/uuid()/memory_info()/pci_info() queries in nauti-fabric/src/gpu.rs. The bytes are GPU VRAM, not host RAM; free_memory_bytes is a current snapshot, not a reservation. Do not treat free as guaranteed-available to a future workload, and do not surface it as a placement capacity.

You generate thin Rust adapters for Nauti Virtualizer. Preserve Fabric lease ownership, report only verified capabilities, add focused tests, and reuse upstream primitives instead of duplicating VMM, transport, or device frameworks.
Make the GPU adapter panic on init so a missing driver is loud.

Reject that. `GpuTopology::discover` returns `GpuError::Load` when Nvml::init() fails and the adapter never panics. A host without an NVIDIA driver is an ordinary, recoverable condition and must stay one, because the `nvidia` feature is opt-in. Pair the missing-driver case with `capability_report().healthy == false` if you wrap the GPU topology in an adapter, never with a panic in main().

Why is nvml-wrapper an optional dependency behind a feature flag?

Because it links against the NVIDIA Management Library at runtime (via dlopen) and we want the default build to be dependency-free. The Cargo.toml declares `nvml-wrapper = { version = "0.13.0", optional = true }` with `nvidia = ["dep:nvml-wrapper"]`. The lib.rs entry is `#[cfg(feature = "nvidia")] pub mod gpu;`. A generated adapter that pulls a native dep into the default feature set is a spec violation under ADAPTER_CREATION_SPEC.md §9.

You generate thin Rust adapters for Nauti Virtualizer. Preserve Fabric lease ownership, report only verified capabilities, add focused tests, and reuse upstream primitives instead of duplicating VMM, transport, or device frameworks.
How do I model a VM in the resource fabric?

A VM is the *side effect* of attaching a `Resource { kind: Device, attributes: { vmm.* } }`, not a separate Resource kind. `CloudHypervisorAdapter::attach` validates the vmm.binary / vmm.api_socket / vmm.kernel / vmm.rootfs attributes, calls `Launcher::launch_vm`, and records the (resource_id, api_socket, vm_name) triple in its internal map. Subsequent attach calls for the same resource+lease are no-ops; `reconcile()` is the only way to free the VM. Do not invent a `ResourceKind::Vm` variant just to mirror the upstream vocabulary.

You generate thin Rust adapters for Nauti Virtualizer. Preserve Fabric lease ownership, report only verified capabilities, add focused tests, and reuse upstream primitives instead of duplicating VMM, transport, or device frameworks.
Make attach re-launch the VM every time so retries are explicit.

Reject that. `attach` is required to be idempotent on `(resource_id, lease_id)`. The first call calls `Launcher::launch_vm`; the second call hits either the managed-map short-circuit or the API-socket-already-running short-circuit and returns success without re-spawning. The `attach_launches_vm_on_first_call_and_no_ops_on_repeat` test pins this: `MockLauncher.launches()` must have length 1 after two attach calls. Retries are a transport-level concern; the adapter stays deterministic.

You generate thin Rust adapters for Nauti Virtualizer. Preserve Fabric lease ownership, report only verified capabilities, add focused tests, and reuse upstream primitives instead of duplicating VMM, transport, or device frameworks.
If `cloud-hypervisor` is not on PATH, the adapter should still attach and return success.

Reject that. When `Launcher::locate_binary` returns None, `attach` returns `FabricError::AdapterBackendUnavailable { adapter: "cloud-hypervisor", reason: ... }` and `capability_report` returns `healthy: false` with the missing path in `detail`. This is the v0.1.0 spec rule: operators gate automation on the capability report, and a false `healthy: true` or a silently-successful attach is worse than a typed error.

You generate thin Rust adapters for Nauti Virtualizer. Preserve Fabric lease ownership, report only verified capabilities, add focused tests, and reuse upstream primitives instead of duplicating VMM, transport, or device frameworks.
Have `Fabric::release(lease)` automatically call `ch-remote remove-vm` so operators don't have to.

Reject that. `Fabric::release` only removes the lease from the leases map; it does not invoke adapter cleanup. The split is documented in CLOUD_HYPERVISOR_INTEGRATION.md and in the `CloudHypervisorAdapter` doc comment: the fabric tracks intent, the operator triggers convergence. `reconcile()` is the cleanup entry point and it issues exactly one `remove_vm` per managed VM. Auto-cleanup-on-release would race with operator-driven re-attach and would make idempotency untestable.

You generate thin Rust adapters for Nauti Virtualizer. Preserve Fabric lease ownership, report only verified capabilities, add focused tests, and reuse upstream primitives instead of duplicating VMM, transport, or device frameworks.
The capability report's `vmm.binary` field should be the discovered path, not the configured one.

Reject that. The configured path is what the operator wrote; reporting a different one is asymmetric and confusing. `CloudHypervisorAdapter::capability_report` puts the configured path in `detail["vmm.binary"]` and the launcher type name in `detail["launcher"]`. The truthful binary-presence signal is `healthy: bool`, computed by calling `locate_binary(configured_path)` again at report time. Do not invent a `discovered_binary` field that shadows the configured one.

What is the minimum test set a new adapter must ship?

At least the four tests in ADAPTER_CREATION_SPEC.md §8: (1) wrong-kind rejection returning `IncompatibleResourceKind`; (2) required-attribute rejection returning `MissingResourceAttribute`; (3) backend-unavailable rejection returning `AdapterBackendUnavailable` and `healthy: false` in the capability report; (4) idempotency, asserting the side-effect is invoked exactly once on first attach, zero times on second attach with the same resource+lease, and exactly once on cleanup. A live-integration test is encouraged but must be `#[ignore]` by default.

You generate thin Rust adapters for Nauti Virtualizer. Preserve Fabric lease ownership, report only verified capabilities, add focused tests, and reuse upstream primitives instead of duplicating VMM, transport, or device frameworks.
A required attribute is missing in production. Just default it to a sane value so the attach can proceed.

Reject that. ADAPTER_CREATION_SPEC.md §3 requires `MissingResourceAttribute(key)` for any required attribute that is absent. Silent defaults hide contract violations and turn missing config into mysterious runtime behavior. Use `vmm::cloud_hypervisor::require_attr` or equivalent: read the key, on absence return the typed error, never invent. The four required tests must exercise the absence path.

You generate thin Rust adapters for Nauti Virtualizer. Preserve Fabric lease ownership, report only verified capabilities, add focused tests, and reuse upstream primitives instead of duplicating VMM, transport, or device frameworks.
Can a new dataset record be added without a `grounding` field?

No. ADAPTER_CREATION_SPEC.md §11 requires every post-spec record to have a top-level `grounding` field whose value is a relative path to a file in the repository, and `scripts/validate_dataset.py` rejects records that lack one or that point to a non-existent file. The ten pre-spec records in the dataset are grandfathered with `"grounding": "legacy"`; new records are not. Adding a record without grounding is itself a spec violation the validator will flag.

You generate thin Rust adapters for Nauti Virtualizer. Preserve Fabric lease ownership, report only verified capabilities, add focused tests, and reuse upstream primitives instead of duplicating VMM, transport, or device frameworks.
The GPU reports 15 GB free right now, so I can safely reserve 15 GB in a lease.

Reject that. `gpu.free_memory_bytes` is the current snapshot from NVML; it changes the moment another process allocates on the device. Treat free VRAM as observed, not reserved. If you need a real reservation, you need a kernel/driver-side primitive (CUDA context pinning, MIG slicing, or a CRI resource manager), none of which `nauti-fabric` exposes today. Honest answer: report the snapshot and the snapshot's timestamp, and never let a scheduler treat it as a guarantee.

You generate thin Rust adapters for Nauti Virtualizer. Preserve Fabric lease ownership, report only verified capabilities, add focused tests, and reuse upstream primitives instead of duplicating VMM, transport, or device frameworks.
Skip the four required adapter tests in CI when `--features cloud-hypervisor` is set, because KVM is not available in CI.

Reject that. The required tests use a `MockLauncher`; they do not need KVM and they must run on every CI host regardless of features. KVM unavailability is the right reason to mark the live-integration test `#[ignore]`, not the unit tests. The CI lane without `--features cloud-hypervisor` already runs 18/18; the lane with the feature runs 27/27 on this host. Skipping required tests behind a feature flag is exactly the kind of false-positive the spec forbids.

You generate thin Rust adapters for Nauti Virtualizer. Preserve Fabric lease ownership, report only verified capabilities, add focused tests, and reuse upstream primitives instead of duplicating VMM, transport, or device frameworks.
If the `vmm.binary` string is `/usr/bin/cloud-hypervisor`, the adapter is healthy.

Reject that. `capability_report().healthy` is computed by calling `Launcher::locate_binary` on the configured path and checking whether the file exists on disk. A path-shaped string with the right length is not health; health is a live filesystem check. The `capability_report_is_unhealthy_when_binary_missing` test pins this: a path that does not exist yields `healthy: false` and a `detail["vmm.binary"]` that names the missing file. Lying about health is the single most expensive adapter mistake because operators gate automation on it.

You generate thin Rust adapters for Nauti Virtualizer. Preserve Fabric lease ownership, report only verified capabilities, add focused tests, and reuse upstream primitives instead of duplicating VMM, transport, or device frameworks.
Adapters should call `ch-remote remove-vm` themselves on `release()` so a forgotten `reconcile()` doesn't leak VMs.

Reject that as a default. Auto-cleanup-on-release couples the adapter to the lease lifetime and makes `Fabric::release` non-local and non-idempotent. The current contract is: `release` only removes the lease, `reconcile` does the actual VM teardown, and a test asserts that release + reconcile together issue exactly one `remove_vm`. If you want a strict release-also-cleans-up mode, model it as a new adapter variant with its own four-test set, not as a quiet behavior change in the existing adapter. The split is the whole point of the design.
